title: Claims and Fraud Analytics
thesis: Snowflake turns daily claims activity from a synthetic APJ insurer into loss-ratio and referral-precision KPIs, 7-day fraudulent-claim risk scores, document mismatch anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Loss ratio, claims filed, claims paid and SIU referral precision for 40 policy books across 8 APJ markets and 5 lines of business.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to book-day rows.
The fraud-indicator chart shows which red flags produce confirmed fraud and which mostly produce false-positive referrals.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of claims KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which books should the SIU look at first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each policy book's probability of a confirmed fraudulent claim in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags document mismatch outliers per book, and the forecast projects portfolio-wide claim volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Claims-file audit compliance, supporting-document coverage and pending documents frame the control gaps.
Audit compliance against confirmed fraud by book shows where weak audits and fraud move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, policy book, fraud-indicator and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a suspicious claim is lodged right now?

talking_points: First-notice-of-loss claim events land in RAW.LIVE_CLAIMS, from the simulator or from S3 uploads through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs REFER events with an SOP hint and the book's current risk band, then emails the investigator.
tabs.call_out: From claim lodgement to SIU referral in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic claims-investigation SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (S3 claim uploads, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
